blocking: The fixed Pause control remains over the footer in desktop screenshot 4, violating the owner's no-controls-over-footer rule.
The hero's 600px minimum height and viewport-based tree positioning diverge on short screens, allowing the canopy to cross hero content.
The desktop sprig crops scale the full artwork to the narrow crop width, breaking their intended registration with the tree.

fixes.what: Move motion-control positioning outside the optional hww-tab block. Give it a reserved area that avoids content and park it above the footer when the footer enters view; preserve keyboard access.
fixes.why: Removing the home tab also bypassed its shared control logic; the fixed button visibly overlays the footer.

fixes.what: Define one effective hero height, including the 600px minimum, and use it consistently for hero layout, tree placement and statement offsets. Check short landscape screens and enlarged text.
fixes.why: The hero grows to 600px while tree placement still uses the shorter viewport height.

fixes.what: Set sprig images to width:var(--tree-w) rather than the inherited width:100%, retaining the existing crop offsets and clipping containers.
fixes.why: Each 470-art-pixel crop currently rescales the entire 1536px artwork before applying full-scale offsets.

fixes.where: assets/js/canopy.js build() scroll-velocity onUpdate and kill()
fixes.what: Track the shake timeline explicitly and revert it in kill(), or create it through a context-bound callback. Reset shaking state during cleanup.
fixes.why: Timelines created later inside onUpdate are not reliably captured by the initial context and can continue after Pause or reduced-motion activation.

fixes.what: Keep content geometry stable when motion is toggled; compensate tree positioning without switching the statement's normal-flow offset, then refresh remaining triggers after cleanup.
fixes.why: Pause currently changes --at-1270 and shifts every subsequent section while the reader is using the page.

fixes.what: Create and retain an empty context before adding animations, wrap construction in try/catch, and revert partial work plus canopy classes on failure.
fixes.why: Unlike site.js, canopy initialization has no safe rollback; a partial failure can leave positioning classes and animations active.
